name: Demi Guard Elevation Sweep
summary: The Demi Guard elevation sweep uses the gi lapel-and-foot connection to lift a forward-pressing passer off balance and come on top while freeing the fabric for stabilization.
description: Demi Guard Elevation Sweep in gi BJJ: learn the starting controls, movement sequence, defensive reactions and recovery options for a connected lapel-guard exchange.
overview:
The elevation opportunity follows from Demi's knee-line lapel connection and the passer's forward pressure. [Legion's definition](https://legionsandiego.com/the-jiu-jitsu-dictionary/#demi-guard) identifies elevation for a sweep, and [Keenan's curriculum](https://jiujitsux.com/courses/keenans-lapel-encyclopedia/lesson/16-1-introduction-to-the-demi-guard/) lists a basic sweep, a lateral tilt and a Demi X variation. This page describes the general elevation-to-top transition, not the detailed sequence of those separate lessons.

A reversal may finish with the opponent retaining [[Positions/Half Guard]] or [[Positions/Open Guard]]. Free the lapel as needed to stabilize rather than assuming that elevation also passed the legs. If the opponent recovers base, retain Demi or recover a guard before their pressure clears your knees.

attacker.name: Demi Guard Elevation Sweep Attacker
attacker.description: Execute Demi Guard Elevation Sweep with the right starting controls, a stable destination and a clear recovery when the attempt is blocked.
attacker.overview: You begin underneath in established Demi Guard. Use the connected collar, lapel and foot to respond to a visible forward weight shift. The goal is to reverse the top-bottom relationship and then stabilize; lifting the knee without changing the opponent's base is not a completed sweep.
key_principles: Start with the full Demi configuration.
Read a weight shift before lifting.
Coordinate collar control with the foot-supported lapel.
Follow the reversal rather than stopping at elevation.
Free obstructing fabric and stabilize the real landing.
setup_requirements: You are in Demi Guard bottom with the lapel behind the knee.
Your foot has useful contact on the lapel tail.
The collar grip remains available to manage the upper body.
The passer's pressure creates a visible change of balance.

execution_steps.description: Check the collar grip, knee-line lapel and foot contact while keeping your legs between your torso and the passer.
Identify the passer's weight moving forward onto the supported leg instead of trying to lift a fully balanced opponent.
Use the working foot-and-lapel connection to elevate the controlled knee, coordinating the movement with the collar connection.
Continue into the space created as the passer loses base; do not force the same motion if they recover a stable post.
Follow the reversal with your hips and torso until you are above the opponent, recognizing any guard their legs retain.
Free fabric that binds your movement and settle top half guard or top open guard before attempting a separate pass.

common_counters.counter: Recover a stable post and center your weight
common_counters.your_response: Keep the remaining guard or base and reassess the controls before repeating the attempt; do not force a knee against the lapel.

common_counters.counter: Reduce the foot-on-lapel load while keeping balance
common_counters.your_response: Keep the remaining guard or base and reassess the controls before repeating the attempt; do not force a knee against the lapel.

common_counters.counter: Clear the legs after the sweep structure collapses
common_counters.your_response: Keep the remaining guard or base and reassess the controls before repeating the attempt; do not force a knee against the lapel.

common_errors.error: Lifting before the passer's weight shifts
common_errors.consequence: You work against a stable base and exhaust the grips.
common_errors.correction: Recognize the forward loading before committing to elevation.

common_errors.error: Pulling only with the collar arm
common_errors.consequence: The knee line stays supported and the passer can recover posture.
common_errors.correction: Coordinate the upper-body connection with the loaded foot and lapel.

common_errors.error: Forcing the sweep against a fixed knee
common_errors.consequence: The fabric can bind the joint while the bodies rotate.
common_errors.correction: Release tension and reset if the leg cannot move comfortably.

common_errors.error: Stopping after the opponent loses balance
common_errors.consequence: The opponent can recover top position before you follow.
common_errors.correction: Continue into a controlled top landing when the base actually gives way.

common_errors.error: Assuming the reversal passed the guard
common_errors.consequence: The opponent's remaining leg trap catches your next movement.
common_errors.correction: Identify half or open guard and stabilize before a separate pass.

training_progressions.description: You are in Demi Guard bottom with the lapel behind the knee. With a cooperative partner, identify the required grips and leg contacts, then reset without applying pressure.
Perform the listed sequence slowly with a cooperative partner. Pause at the change of lapel or foot control and reset on any joint discomfort.
Let the partner use this response: Recover a stable post and center your weight. Practice keeping a safe base or guard when it blocks the attempt, then reset.
Start at the stated origin with light resistance. Stop and reset at a stable destination, a counter, or a request to release; do not continue through a bound knee.

flashcards.question: What passer reaction supplies the Demi elevation opportunity?
flashcards.answer: Forward pressure can load the foot-supported lapel connection, allowing elevation when the passer's base begins to shift.

flashcards.question: What must work with the collar grip during a Demi sweep?
flashcards.answer: The foot and lapel behind the opponent's knee must coordinate with the collar connection to affect both the base and upper body.

flashcards.question: What is missing if you elevate the knee but remain underneath?
flashcards.answer: The reversal is incomplete; you still need to follow the change of base and establish a stable position on top.

flashcards.question: Why might a successful Demi sweep land in top half guard?
flashcards.answer: Reversing the players does not guarantee leg clearance; the opponent can retain one of your legs as you come on top.

flashcards.question: What should you do if the lapel binds your landing?
flashcards.answer: Release the fabric that obstructs stabilization rather than turning against a trapped leg or chasing an immediate pass.

attacker.safety_considerations: Use controlled pressure with a cooperative partner when learning the lapel path. Release fabric immediately on a tap, verbal stop or discomfort. Do not rotate against a knee held by the lapel, and stop the drill when a stable landing is reached.

defender.name: Demi Guard Elevation Sweep Defender
defender.description: Recognize and respond to Demi Guard Elevation Sweep while protecting balance, remaining frames and a safe recovery route.
defender.overview: You are the passer whose forward weight is being loaded onto the guard player's connection. Recover balance while the knee is still free to move, and reduce the foot-on-lapel barrier. If the reversal occurs, recover guard on landing rather than trying to save the exchange through a trapped joint.
key_principles: Recognize the change of collar, lapel and foot controls early.
Keep a usable base or leg barrier while contesting the movement.
Choose a response that fits the current controls rather than a lost grip.
Release any connection that binds a knee during movement.
Identify the resulting position before continuing the exchange.
recognition_cues: Your controlled knee begins to rise with the lapel-supported foot.
The collar connection draws your torso into the changing base.
The guard player follows the elevation to come up rather than staying flat.

defensive_options.action: Recover a stable post and center your weight
defensive_options.when_to_use: Before the elevation carries your hips beyond your base
defensive_options.if_successful: You remain on top while the bottom player retains Demi.
defensive_options.risk: A late post may not stop the reversal.

defensive_options.action: Reduce the foot-on-lapel load while keeping balance
defensive_options.when_to_use: When you feel the controlled knee beginning to lift
defensive_options.if_successful: The sweep stalls and the position remains contested.
defensive_options.risk: Reaching without base can supply the missing weight shift.

defensive_options.action: Clear the legs after the sweep structure collapses
defensive_options.when_to_use: Only after the collar and leg barrier no longer stop your advance
defensive_options.if_successful: You complete the counter-pass and settle side control.
defensive_options.risk: Driving before the connection is cleared can restart the elevation.

favorable_outcomes.how: Recover a stable post and center your weight. You remain on top while the bottom player retains Demi.
Reduce the foot-on-lapel load while keeping balance. The sweep stalls and the position remains contested.
Clear the legs after the sweep structure collapses. You complete the counter-pass and settle side control.

common_errors.error: Responding after the new controls are established
common_errors.consequence: The attacker completes the movement before the response affects it.
common_errors.correction: Recognize the listed cues during the control change.

common_errors.error: Turning against a knee still bound by the lapel
common_errors.consequence: The joint cannot follow the body movement freely.
common_errors.correction: Release binding tension and reset rather than forcing the turn.

common_errors.error: Ignoring the position left after the attempt
common_errors.consequence: You continue with a response intended for a guard that has already changed.
common_errors.correction: Check the actual leg and upper-body controls before the next action.

flashcards.question: What is the first aim when a Demi sweep starts elevating your knee?
flashcards.answer: Recover a stable base and reduce the loaded foot-and-lapel connection while the leg can still move comfortably.

flashcards.question: Why can an early forward drive worsen the Demi sweep threat?
flashcards.answer: It brings more weight onto the bottom player's supported connection before you have removed the structure producing elevation.

flashcards.question: What should you seek if the Demi sweep has already reversed you?
flashcards.answer: Recover a guard as you land and protect your base, instead of twisting a bound knee to prevent an already-completed reversal.

training_progressions.description: From the stated origin, have the partner begin slowly. Call out a listed recognition cue, then release and reset.
Recover a stable post and center your weight. Use light resistance and stop when the response succeeds or the connection becomes uncomfortable.
Let the partner choose whether to continue or recover. Respond using the available controls; stop at the resulting stable position and name both players' roles.
